claims.claim: Stories must leave the Realms as found: no destroying or irrevocably changing established places, peoples, or gods without dispensation.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: The guide instructs writers and artists to represent the Realms' many skin tones and ethnic analogs, including in cosmopolitan cities.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: Men and women are depicted equally in all roles; sexist clichés (damsel, sexy barmaid) are banned, with orcs and Northlanders as the two exceptions.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: Sex, romance, and gore are kept PG in Realms products.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: In-world characters speak of time loosely ('mid morning', 'nigh sunset') and, where clocks exist, in 'bells', not o'clock.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: Days of the tenday are 'first day', 'second day', and so on; there is no weekend.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

claims.claim: The Realms guide bans a.m./p.m., coffee (kaeth), money (coin), restaurant (feasting hall), week (tenday), hourglass (sandglass), o'clock (bells), and generic subrace names.
claims.source: Forgotten Realms Style Guide (Wizards of the Coast, bundle document)

verdicts.trueWording: Stories should leave the Realms as they found them.
verdicts.note: p.1 'Replace Your Divots': quote exact. All limbs on page — 'should not definitively destroy or irrevocably change locations, people, gods, planes, races as a whole, or other established elements of the setting or brand without special dispensation.' Only shading: guide says 'should', claim says 'must'; guide also allows high stakes provided 'there must always be the option of things being restored to order.'

verdicts.trueWording: Art must represent the Realms' real range of skin tones.
verdicts.note: p.1-2 header exact. Section enumerates skin tones (sun elves bronze, wild elves dark brown, gold dwarves brown, strongheart halflings dusky) and earth analogs (Chult/Turmish black, Kara-Tur Asian, Calimshan Arab, Amn/Tethyr Spaniard), and the cosmopolitan-city limb is explicit: 'When you set something in Waterdeep, the most cosmopolitan city in the world, there absolutely should be humans from all over the Realms.' Artists limb supported by 'art has failed to consistently and appropriately represent the people of the Forgotten Realms.'

verdicts.trueWording: Males and females depicted in equal measure; two exceptions.
verdicts.note: p.2 'Gender Roles': quote exact. 'males and females should be depicted in equal measure and doing all the same jobs in equal status'; cliche list names 'the damsel in distress, the sexy barmaid'; 'There are two exceptions: orcs and Northlanders.' Guide word is 'Avoid', not 'banned'; the two exceptions as elaborated concern gendered division of labour (orc females stay behind, Northlander women stay home), not licence to use the cliches.

verdicts.trueWording: Keep it PG for both sex and gore.
verdicts.note: 'Keep it PG.' appears twice, exact: p.2 'Sex and Sexuality' bullet (romance covered — 'Depictions of sex and romance between characters should be rare') and p.2 'Violence and Gore' ('As a rule of thumb, keep it PG'). Gore carries a stated exception: 'Occasionally more gore will be called for... but ask before you take gore into the R-rated range.'

verdicts.trueWording: People use loose times; clock hours are called bells.
verdicts.note: p.11 'Keeping Time': quote exact — 'People are accustomed to loose times like “mid morning” or “nigh sunset.”' Bells limb explicit: 'If a local temple or civic structure has a clock, people refer to hours as “bells,” as in “I’ll meet you at seven bells.”' The not-o'clock limb is confirmed by the p.25 Banned Words entry 'o’clock (should be “bells” but most people don’t reference time so specifically)'.

verdicts.trueWording: Tenday days are counted; no concept of the weekend.
verdicts.note: p.11 'Time and the Calendar': quote exact. 'days of the tenday are denoted by counting from the beginning of the tenday. For example, “first day,” “second day,” “third day,” and so on (or alternatively “one-day,” “two-day” etc.). There is no concept of the weekend as a special time when businesses close or people stop work.' Both limbs exact.

verdicts.trueWording: Banned Words list carries every term the claim names.
verdicts.note: p.25 'Banned Words' list verbatim: a.m.; coffee (should be “kaeth” or “kaethae”); money (should be “coin”); restaurant (should be “feasting hall,” or more formally as “skaethar”); week (should be “tenday”); high elf (refer to the Forgotten Realms subraces); hill dwarf (should be “shield dwarf”); hourglass (should be “sandglass”); mountain dwarf (should be “gold dwarf”); o’clock (should be “bells”...); p.m. The generic-subrace limb = the high elf / hill dwarf / mountain dwarf entries. Provenance note only: the cited quote 'tenday (never week)' is verbatim but sits in the alphabetical Terms list (T section, p.27), not in the p.25 Banned Words block, which reads 'week (should be “tenday”)'.
Forgotten Realms Terms, G section: 'godsforsaken (replaces Godforsaken)' — exact, capital G on the replaced word. Adjacent entry 'gold (not money)' corroborates claim 355's money/coin limb.

verdicts.trueWording: goodsir not capped; Goodman/Goodwoman usually capped.
verdicts.note: Forgotten Realms Terms, G section, two consecutive entries: 'Goodman/Goodwoman (a title or form of address, usu. capped)' and 'goodsir (a form of address, not capped)'. Both limbs exact, including the 'usu.' hedge the claim renders as 'usually'.

verdicts.trueWording: Common is a pidgin-derived trade tongue, simpler and less expressive.
verdicts.note: p.14 'The Common Tongue': quote exact. 'Common grew from a kind of pidgin Chondathan... but it is far simpler and less expressive. Nuances of speech, naming, and phrasing are better conveyed in the older, more mature languages, since Common is little more than a trade language.' Accent limb tracks the regional tongues, not Common: 'Other languages might be used to inform an accent or provide a necessary language barrier' — stated for electronic games and film, where Common is assumed to be English.

verdicts.trueWording: 'Forgotten Realms Phrases' lists greetings and farewells.
verdicts.note: p.14 section 'Forgotten Realms Phrases' — 'Below are some phrases common to speah [sic] in the Forgotten Realms.' Quote exact: 'Well met. The most often used greeting, particularly between strangers of a different race or those of whom one is unsure.' Farewell limb exact: 'Until swords part. Warriors’ farewell throughout the Realms.' Also lists Well again, Olore, Aluve, Amarast, Alavairthae, and racial farewells.

verdicts.trueWording: Don't explain everything by exposition, but do inform players.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: 'not use exposition to explain the world' — the guide's ban is on explaining EVERYTHING, and in the same breath it requires the opposite of the claim's blanket: 'but do inform the players about the world. Don’t assume they come to the IP with complete knowledge.'
verdicts.note: p.1, guideline 3: 'Stay experiential. Don’t attempt to use exposition to explain everything in the IP, but do inform the players about the world.' The two-word quote is exact and the experiential limb holds, but the claim drops both the 'everything' quantifier and the mandatory counter-clause, converting a calibrated instruction into a blanket prohibition the page contradicts.

verdicts.trueWording: Mostly, monsters are for killing, and their stuff is for taking.
verdicts.note: p.2 'Monsters': quote exact. Exception limb explicit: 'They can also occasionally play non-combat roles opposing or aiding the players (the helpful kobold, the hobgoblin informant, the doppelganger spy), but such instances are out of character for D&D and require explanation.' Also 'Monsters should be the bulk of combat foes players face.'

verdicts.trueWording: Must use the template; should know the D&D Style Guide.
verdicts.note: p.1, 'TECHNICAL INFORMATION': quote exact. Version limb exact — 'Effective Date: May 2025. Version 1.9c (updated June 23, 2025)'. Template limb is the strongest — 'You must use this template and follow the formatting standards as presented in the template.' Style guide limb is 'You should be familiar with the D&D Style Guide (also provided) as well'; the DMsGuild limb is worded as review, not familiarity — 'Please review the Wizards and the DMsGuild Content Guidelines.'

verdicts.trueWording: Adventures must use the template provided.
verdicts.note: Quote exact, in 'THE FINE PRINT' (p.8), corroborated on p.1 by 'You must use this template' and 'Your adventure must follow the template provided for layout'. Accessible-version limb exact, p.1 'Accessibility': 'The template must be one of your downloads, adjusted to use tags, bookmarks, alt text... Additionally, you may create a version that does not use the template, using fonts, sizing, formatting, and layout as advised by accessibility experts.' — so the non-template version is permitted alongside, not instead of, the template.
